implementation_notes: Default Kotlin realization on a JMS broker: identical to the Java API surface, with Kotlin's SAM conversion for the MessageListener. Choose it when the broker is a JMS provider and subscription lifecycle should be managed through the standard API.
code_sketch:
connection.clientID = "billing-ledger"
val session = connection.createSession(false, Session.CLIENT_ACKNOWLEDGE)
val sub = session.createDurableSubscriber(topic, "billing-ledger")
sub.messageListener = MessageListener { m ->
    handle(m)          // idempotent
    m.acknowledge()    // drains the retained backlog
}
connection.start()
pitfalls: Blocking listener callbacks run on the provider's thread; long work there stalls the connection's delivery.
Changing clientID or subscription name leaves an orphan subscription retaining messages.

variants.name: Kafka consumer group with manual commitSync
variants.implementation_notes: Where Kafka is the broker, the group id is the durable identity and committed offsets are the retained position; Kotlin services typically poll inside a coroutine and commit after handling. Choose it when replay from a shared log matters more than broker-managed subscriptions.
pitfalls: commitSync inside the poll loop blocks; batch the commits and accept replay of the last batch.
Offsets only survive as long as the group and offset retention do.
